system_description.narrative_title: Fragmented Global Order: War, Energy Shocks and a Bond Rout
system_description.narrative_summary: The international system is an open, tightly coupled process: regional wars (Ukraine, Middle East, Horn of Africa) drive energy and trade shocks that cascade into global commodity and financial markets, while high inflation and rising yields strain public finances and domestic politics. Great‑power competition (US, China, Russia) and alliance management shape responses—oil stock releases, naval deployments, sanctions—creating feedbacks that amplify instability and policy tradeoffs across markets, borders and institutions.
system_description.scope: Interacting transnational processes among sovereign states, defence forces, energy and commodity flows, international capital markets and central banks, alliance institutions (G7, EU, NATO), and major domestic political cycles and elections.
system_description.super_system: The international political‑economic order of states, markets and multilateral institutions embedded in planetary resource and security constraints.
adjacent_subsystems: Global energy and commodity markets (oil, diesel, LNG, food)
International financial markets and central banking (sovereign yields, bond markets)
Regional security complexes (Europe/Ukraine, Middle East, Horn of Africa)
Great‑power strategic competition and alliance politics (US–China–Russia and partners)

variables.name: Russia–Ukraine war and escalation
variables.description: Russia and Ukraine, backed respectively by a changing mix of Western military aid and asymmetric Ukrainian countermeasures, are locked in a sustained war whose tactics and intensity are evolving and driving deeper allied support and strategic recalculations.

variables.name: Hormuz and Red Sea maritime tensions
variables.description: Iran, Houthi forces, regional navies and the US/Saudi security presence are clashing at key sea lanes, producing repeated attacks on vessels and a persistent deterioration in maritime security around Hormuz and the Red Sea.

variables.name: Global diesel and fuel supply shock
variables.description: Major consuming and producing states and blocs (G7, EU, US, China, OPEC+) are responding to acute diesel and refined-fuel shortages with coordinated reserve releases, export curbs and refinery adjustments, shifting short-term market balances and political stress around energy affordability.

variables.name: Global bond sell-off and rising yields
variables.description: Sovereign borrowers, investors and central banks in the US, euro area and other developed markets face a sharp, multi-market rise in yields that is reshaping monetary policy expectations, funding costs and fiscal stress across economies.

variables.name: US–China strategic competition in the Indo‑Pacific
variables.description: The United States, China and regional actors (Taiwan, Japan, Philippines, South Korea and ASEAN states) are contesting military postures, trade and technological influence across the Indo‑Pacific, driving force realignments and decoupling pressures.
